issues.t: Plastic intake manifold cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant dripping or spraying from the front top of the engine near the thermostat, a sweet smell, the temperature gauge climbing, or a sudden overheat.
issues.why: The all-plastic intake manifold on the 4.6L V8 has a coolant passage at the front that cracks with age and heat. Ford extended coverage and reimbursed some owners years ago.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs. Replace the manifold with the updated design that has an aluminum coolant crossover.

issues.t: Rear air suspension sags or compressor fails
issues.sym: The rear of the car sits low after parking, a "check suspension" light comes on, the ride turns bouncy, or the compressor runs for a long time.
issues.why: The rear air springs crack and leak with age. The compressor then runs too much and wears out, and the air dryer can fail as well.
issues.next: Have the springs and dryer leak-tested before replacing the compressor. Turn the air suspension switch in the trunk off before jacking the car. Coil-spring conversion kits are another option.

issues.t: Coolant leak at the front of the intake manifold
issues.sym: A small coolant puddle or crusty residue at the front of the engine near the thermostat housing, and a coolant level that slowly drops.
issues.why: The updated intake manifold still uses a plastic body with a coolant passage at the front. It can crack or leak where it joins the coolant crossover.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level. Have the leak traced with a pressure test before it turns into an overheat.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: Slipping, delayed or harsh shifts, the engine revving without the car speeding up, or no movement in Drive.
issues.why: Internal wear in the 4-speed automatic. CarComplaints owners report failures at around 64,000 miles on 2004 cars.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis before the damage grows.

issues.t: Feels sluggish or shifts up too early
issues.sym: The car feels like it lacks power or the transmission shifts into higher gears too soon.
issues.why: A check ball in the transmission valve body can upset the torque converter clutch control.
issues.next: Ask a shop familiar with Ford transmissions to check the valve body. It is not an emergency but should be fixed before it wears the converter.

issues.t: Spark plug blown out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud popping or ticking from one side of the engine, a misfire and a check engine light.
issues.why: The 4.6L heads hold each spark plug with only a few threads in soft aluminum. The threads can let go and the plug is pushed out.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as it is safe. A shop can usually install a thread insert without removing the head.

issues.t: Heater core leaks
issues.sym: A sweet smell inside, fogged windows, damp front carpet, or coolant loss with no leak under the hood.
issues.why: The heater core can leak repeatedly on these cars. Ford suggested a restrictor in the heater inlet hose to reduce pressure on the core.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Replace the core and ask for the hose restrictor so the new core lasts.

issues.t: Power windows stop working
issues.sym: A window goes up or down slowly, makes a grinding noise, drops into the door, or will not move at all.
issues.why: The window regulator cable or motor wears out.
issues.next: Have the door panel removed and the regulator and motor checked. Replacing both together is common.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder fails
issues.sym: The brake pedal sinks slowly to the floor or feels soft, and stops get longer.
issues.why: Internal seals in the brake master cylinder wear and let fluid bypass.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have the brakes checked right away. A sinking pedal is a safety issue.

issues.t: Ticking engine noise at idle
issues.sym: A light ticking from the top of the engine at idle.
issues.why: Some engines from these years developed a valvetrain tick. In some cases the cylinder head and camshaft had to be replaced.
issues.next: Check the oil level and have the noise diagnosed. Keep up with oil changes.

issues.t: Keyless remote and door keypad stop working
issues.sym: The key fob and door keypad stop locking or unlocking the doors.
issues.why: A short in the wiring, usually under a front seat.
issues.next: Have the wiring under the seats checked before replacing modules.

issues.t: Blower fan quits or changes speed on its own
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan stops working or changes speed without you touching the controls.
issues.why: A wiring harness problem in the blower circuit. A new harness is sometimes needed.
issues.next: Have the blower circuit checked. It is a comfort problem, but a fan that stops can make defrosting harder.

issues.t: Radiator fan stops, causing overheating and weak A/C
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs in traffic and the A/C blows less cold when the car is stopped.
issues.why: The electric radiator fan motor can fail.
issues.next: Pull over if the gauge goes into the red. Have the fan motor and its wiring tested.

issues.t: Water leaks into the trunk
issues.sym: Water in the trunk floor or spare tire area, especially after opening the trunk in the rain.
issues.why: Water runs in through drain holes when the trunk lid is opened. Sealing the holes with foam-backed tape is the fix.
issues.next: Dry the trunk and have the drain holes sealed to stop rust and mildew.

issues.t: Rear wheels chatter in slow turns
issues.sym: A chattering or shuddering from the rear when turning slowly, such as in a parking lot.
issues.why: The clutch pack in the limited-slip rear differential wears or the fluid breaks down.
issues.next: Have the differential fluid and friction additive changed. If it still chatters, a revised clutch pack may be needed.

issues.t: Delay before Reverse engages
issues.sym: Up to about two seconds before the car moves after shifting into Reverse.
issues.why: A weak detent spring or a shift cable that is out of adjustment.
issues.next: Have the shift cable adjustment and detent spring checked; it is a simple fix.

issues.t: Airbag or seat belt warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag light or seat belt warning light stays on, sometimes with a chime.
issues.why: Faults in seat belt buckle sensors, seat wiring or the occupant sensing system.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. Airbags may not work as intended while the light is on.

issues.t: Serpentine belt slips off in wet weather
issues.sym: A squeal followed by the battery light, overheating or heavy steering after driving through water or rain.
issues.why: Water can make the accessory belt walk off its pulleys. A redesigned water pump, tensioner pulley or both were the fix.
issues.next: If the belt comes off, stop: the water pump and alternator are no longer turning. Have the pulleys checked for the updated parts.

issues.t: Long crank or stall from sticking idle air valve
issues.sym: The engine cranks for a long time before starting, or starts and then stalls.
issues.why: The idle air control valve can stick with carbon.
issues.next: Have the idle air valve cleaned or replaced.

issues.t: Squeal from belt tensioner or idler pulley on cold starts
issues.sym: A squeal or chirp from the front of the engine on cold mornings that fades as it warms.
issues.why: Bearings in the belt tensioner or idler pulley wear.
issues.next: Have the pulleys spun by hand to find the noisy one and replace it with a new belt.

issues.t: Rattle or buzz from exhaust heat shields
issues.sym: A rattle or buzz from under the car, often at idle or at certain engine speeds.
issues.why: Heat shields on the catalytic converter and muffler work loose. A rough idle vibration on these years was also fixed with a damper on the Y-pipe.
issues.next: Have the shields re-secured with clamps; it is a simple fix.

issues.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some owners notice a burning smell or smoke near the brake master cylinder, even with the car off.
issues.why: The switch that shuts off cruise control when you brake can leak brake fluid inside itself and overheat.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recall 07V-336. If the fused harness was never added, park outside until it is done.

issues.t: Rusted steering shaft can cause loss of steering (recall)
issues.sym: Steering that feels notchy, binds or clunks, or in the worst case stops responding.
issues.why: Corrosion can seize the lower bearing of the intermediate steering shaft. A follow-up recall covered shafts that were not fixed correctly the first time.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 13V-385 and 14V-704. Do not drive if the steering binds.

issues.t: Battery cable can chafe and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; possibly a burning smell or electrical problems.
issues.why: A fusible link on the battery cable can rub against a crossmember bolt, wear through and overheat.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recall 05V-518 and have the cable rerouted or replaced.

issues.t: Front wheel hub can fracture (recall)
issues.sym: A grinding or clunking from a front wheel, or a wheel that wobbles.
issues.why: Some front wheel bearing and hub assemblies were not heat-treated properly and can crack, which could let the wheel come off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 07V-270 and have both front hubs inspected.

issues.t: Lower ball joint can crack on limousines and fleet cars (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front over bumps, loose steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: On heavy-duty fleet and limousine versions, a one-piece ball joint bearing can weaken and crack, letting the control arm drop.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 98V-322 and have the front ball joints inspected.

issues.t: Rear brake lines can rub through (campaign)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking near the rear of the car, a brake warning light, or a soft pedal.
issues.why: Some brake lines did not have enough clearance and can wear through, letting fluid escape from the rear brakes.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for campaign 98I-001. Have the lines inspected and any worn sections replaced.

issues.t: Rear axle shaft can break on fleet cars (recall)
issues.sym: A growl or grinding from the rear wheels, then a sudden loss of drive.
issues.why: Heavy fleet use overloads the rear wheel bearings. A failed bearing can lead to the axle shaft breaking.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 04V-328, especially on former livery or fleet cars.

issues.t: Driver door latch may open in a side crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in daily driving; the risk is the door opening in a side impact.
issues.why: When the door is closed only to the second latch position, the latch may not be strong enough.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 96V-070 and always shut the door firmly.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not be bolted in place (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: Two bolts that attach the driver airbag to the steering wheel were left out on some cars, so the airbag may not stay in place when it deploys.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 96V-231 and have the airbag mounting checked.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle may not latch or hold (recalls)
issues.sym: A front seat belt that does not click in fully, or comes unlatched with a tug.
issues.why: Some buckles were not heat-treated properly or do not latch fully, so they may not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 00V-228 and 01V-227 and have the buckles replaced.

issues.t: Airbag control module may fail to detect faults (recalls)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag light, or no symptom at all.
issues.why: A restraint control module may not detect certain faults, and some modules were missing mounting screws. Either can affect how airbags deploy.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 00V-270 and 00V-412 and have the module inspected.

issues.t: Wiper motor switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers stop working, or a burning smell near the base of the windshield.
issues.why: A switch inside the wiper motor gear case can overheat, causing the wipers to quit or a fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the wiper motor recall and have the motor repaired.

issues.t: Fuel may leak near the intake manifold (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell under the hood.
issues.why: On a small number of cars, fuel could leak near the intake manifold shield, close to ignition sources.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 10V-638. If you smell fuel, do not drive until it is inspected.
